headline: Initial cold-shock responses can be hazardous even at 10 °C, and hyperventilation did not blunt them.
implication: Supports first-exposure and breathing-safety cautions.
caveat: Small laboratory safety physiology study; not an efficacy source.

headline: A 2026 randomized duration trial found acute mood improvement after 5–20 minutes of 13.6 °C CWI.

caveat: Single immediate outcome, natural setting, self-reported low mood, and limited HRV subgroup.

headline: Three weeks of repeated 7 °C CWI had no clear relevant leukocyte effect and uncertain cardiovascular interpretation.

headline: A single 13.6 °C seawater immersion improved immediate mood scores in young healthy students.

caveat: Natural setting, young sample, and single-session design limit generalization.

headline: Cochrane recovery evidence suggests soreness relief but with low-quality, heterogeneous trials and weak safety reporting.
implication: Useful as adjacent sports-recovery context and as a caveat source, not as a direct wellness cold-plunge claim.
caveat: Post-exercise DOMS studies do not establish benefits for resting cold plunges or broad health outcomes.

headline: Direct 10 °C CWI showed a delayed negative-mood/cortisol signal but mixed cardiovascular and mood endpoints.

headline: The 2025 review is useful landscape evidence, but findings are mixed and heterogeneous.
